content.report:
# Aaron Churba — professional buying-committee profile Research cutoff: 2026-08-27. I treated the supplied LinkedIn URL and the employment-history lock as the identity key. Sensitive material was not collected or reported. ## 1. Identity confirmation Confirmed subject. The supplied LinkedIn profile is titled “Aaron Churba” and says “Director of Sales & Development at Probook”; its employment entry says “Director of Sales & Development - Probook (Current)” and “Feb 2026 - Present.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/aaronloganchurba A first-party announcement by Aaron, dated June 16, 2026, says: “I'm excited to share that I've joined Probook as Director of Sales & Development.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_excited-to-finally-share-what-ive-been-activity-7472702212801056768-sbVT Probook’s own announcement, dated June 27, 2026, says: “We’re excited to welcome Aaron Churba to Probook as our Director of Sales & Development.” It also says he will help “get more businesses to discover Probook,” communicate value, and support/coach the growing GTM team. URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/probook-ai_ten-years-ago-our-cro-mark-hoffman-hired-activity-7472694957506707456-MK6f Same-name people encountered and excluded. * “Aaron Churba” in Florida corporate-registry search results is listed as a registered agent for “Sandals for You 007, L.L.C.” with a Florida address and a 2007 filing date; it has no match to the locked Probook/Bite/Zip Security/Electric history, so I excluded it. URL: https://opengovus.com/florida-corporation/P04000021150
* The same Florida-registry record also appears in a separate “Sandals 4 Events Inc” result; again, there is no matching professional history, so I excluded it. URL: https://opengovus.com/florida-corporation/P08000045694
* No other exact-name professional profile with the locked employment sequence was identified in the returned results. Similar-name results such as Andrew Frydman, David Golub, Michael Slade, Jake Ben-Ami, and Rohan Bakshi were different names and were not treated as same-name candidates. ## 2. Career Dates below are the dates explicitly surfaced by the subject’s LinkedIn profile. Where the profile did not state responsibilities, I mark them NOT FOUND rather than infer them. * Probook — Director of Sales & Development — Feb 2026–present. Aaron’s profile says: “Currently leading a team of 5 sellers and counting.” It describes Probook as “The AI Operating System for Home Services” and says the product is built around dispatch and intended to drive “revenue growth, improve operational efficiency, and add points to their EBITDA.” Aaron says his objectives are “helping more businesses discover Probook, building a world-class GTM organization, and contributing to the next stage of growth.” Probook says his remit includes getting businesses to discover Probook, communicating value clearly, and giving the growing GTM team “support and coaching.”
* Bite — Director of Sales — May 2024–Aug 2025. The profile says he was “Overseeing the sales team at Bite,” focused on “driving sales, nurturing client relationships, and achieving high growth revenue numbers.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/aaronloganchurba
* Bite — Advisor — Aug 2025–Feb 2026. The profile lists “Advisor” at Bite for this period. Specific responsibilities are NOT FOUND.
* Techvera — Sales / Senior Account Executive — Aug 2025–Jan 2026 (the search extract labels the role “Sales”; a Techvera announcement calls him “Senior Account Executive”). Techvera’s announcement says: “Please join us in saying hello to: Aaron Churba, Senior Account Executive.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gabrielsierranyc_techvera-tulsa-msp-activity-7362095842125574144-0T0t. The profile extract does not explain responsibilities. NOT FOUND beyond the title.
* Zip Security — Director of Sales — Jun 2023–May 2024. The profile lists this title and period. Specific responsibilities are NOT FOUND.
* Zip Security — Advisor — Sep 2022–Jun 2023. The profile lists “Advisor.” Specific responsibilities are NOT FOUND.
* Electric — Manager, Sales — May 2022–Jun 2023. Aaron’s profile says he was “One of the early sales hires and a consistent top performer,” was “Promoted to running a team of sellers while continuously exceeding sales targets on an individual basis,” and was part of the Series A–D fundraising rounds.
* Electric — Senior Account Executive — Jan 2022–May 2022. The profile identifies him as “President’s Club Member FY 2021 (Inaugural Year).”
* Electric — Account Executive — Jan 2019–Jan 2022. The profile lists the role; detailed responsibilities are NOT FOUND.
* VTS, Inc. — Business Development — Aug 2017–Jan 2019. The profile lists the role; detailed responsibilities are NOT FOUND.
* SinglePlatform — Senior Business Analyst — May 2016–Aug 2017. The profile lists the role; detailed responsibilities are NOT FOUND. Outbound sales, demand generation, ABM, target-account lists, and GTM tooling. Evidence supports sales leadership, business development, and GTM-team building: Aaron’s current stated goal is “building a world-class GTM organization,” and Probook is hiring SDRs, Commercial AEs, Strategic AEs, and Solutions Consultants. His Electric profile says he ran sellers and exceeded sales targets. Explicit evidence of a named outbound methodology, demand-generation program, ABM process, target-account-list construction, or sales-development software/tooling is NOT FOUND in the sources reviewed. ## 3. Education * Penn State University — Bachelor’s Degree, Telecommunications — 2012–2016. URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/aaronloganchurba
* Nova Southeastern University Shepard Broad College of Law — Master of Science (MS), Law — 2018–2022. The profile describes him as “pursuing a Master of Science - MS focused in Law”; the structured profile reports 2018–2022.
* Post-graduate professional programmes, certificates, or other continuing education: NOT FOUND. ## 4. Public writing, talks, and podcasts The following publicly indexed authored posts were found; no independently indexed bylines, webinars, panels, or podcast appearances were found. * “In my ~10 year journey in SaaS sales, one key lesson stands out…” — LinkedIn, June 26, 2024. Aaron writes: “prospects buy from people they like, relate to, or aspire to emulate.” He extends the point to sales-rep/leader relationships, saying alignment in “values, goals, and communication styles” matters and that hitting targets is “a huge component.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_saassales-salesleadership-relationshipbuilding-activity-7211858644965978113-UIvD
* “Bite’s Kiosk Solution enhances guest experiences, reduces labor costs, and boosts restaurant sales…” — LinkedIn, Aug. 21, 2024. The post describes Bite’s kiosk value proposition and thanks 858 Partners and California Fish Grill. URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_bites-kiosk-solution-enhances-guest-experiences-activity-7232014464059863040-4nV2
* “The companies that get most from their technology aren’t spending more, they’re planning with precision.” — LinkedIn, Nov. 12, 2025. The indexed extract begins: “I talk a lot with business leaders…”; the complete substantive text is NOT FOUND in the returned evidence. URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_2026-it-security-budget-planning-activity-7394430474065956865-UUuf
* “Just a short 3.5 years ago I was laid off. I had no idea what was next.” — LinkedIn, Mar. 29, 2022. Aaron describes calling Matt Deis about Electric and says: “Fast forward 3.5 years later, Electric is a unicorn.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_just-a-short-35-years-ago-i-was-laid-off-activity-6914610056449679361-UPhs
* “Excited to (finally) share what I’ve been working over the past few months.” — LinkedIn, June 16, 2026. This is his Probook announcement and says he is focused on discovery, GTM organization-building, and growth. Most substantive quote. “In my ~10 year journey in SaaS sales, one key lesson stands out: prospects buy from people they like, relate to, or aspire to emulate.” ## 5. What Aaron owns at Probook today Publicly evidenced scope: sales and development; a current team of “5 sellers and counting”; helping more businesses discover Probook; building a “world-class GTM organization”; clearly communicating value; and supporting/coaching the growing GTM team. Direct reports: Public evidence says he leads “a team of 5 sellers and counting.” Names and exact reporting lines are NOT FOUND. Open roles reporting into him: Probook’s careers page lists “Founding Account Executive” under Sales. URL: https://www.probook.ai/careers. Probook’s company page lists GTM openings “Sales Development Representative” and “Enterprise Account Executive.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/company. The pages do not explicitly say that these roles report to Aaron; therefore reporting relationship is NOT FOUND. What he says he is building: “helping more businesses discover Probook, building a world-class GTM organization, and contributing to the next stage of growth.” A customer case-study page quotes Ryan Laske saying: “When Aaron and I tell new prospective hires we’re dispatching based on objective metrics, we see that those who react positively end up being true A players.” This supports a public hiring/operating emphasis on objective dispatch metrics, but it is a customer-side quote rather than Aaron’s own direct statement. URL: https://www.probook.ai/case-studies/tr-miller ## 6. How they think and buy Evaluation/buying evidence: Aaron publicly says, “The companies that get most from their technology aren’t spending more, they’re planning with precision.” This indicates a stated preference for disciplined technology planning rather than simply higher spend. Specific procurement process, buying committee, ROI model, security review, implementation criteria, or software-selection checklist: NOT FOUND. Tools publicly praised or criticised: No named sales, marketing, CRM, prospecting, ABM, or GTM tools were found in the reviewed sources. NOT FOUND. Methodologies: No named sales methodology or ABM methodology was found. NOT FOUND. Metrics: His LinkedIn profile references “achieving high growth revenue numbers” at Bite, “continuously exceeding sales targets” at Electric, and leading five sellers at Probook. Probook’s public positioning emphasizes customer “measurable value,” revenue growth, operational efficiency, and EBITDA improvement. The Probook case study uses “objective metrics” in dispatch/hiring context. Communication style: Relationship-led and alignment-oriented. Aaron writes that prospects buy from people they “like, relate to, or aspire to emulate,” and that alignment in “values, goals, and communication styles” creates “palpable” synergy. ## 7. Non-sensitive personal hooks * Penn State connection: His profile lists Penn State University, Telecommunications, 2012–2016.
* Sales achievement: He identifies as “President’s Club Member FY 2021 (Inaugural Year)” and “President’s Club Member FY 2022.”
* Longstanding professional relationship: Aaron says Mark Hoffman hired him “into my first job out of college” ten years before the Probook announcement, and that returning to work with Mark was a meaningful reason for joining.
* Publicly stated interests/hobbies, sports, volunteering, side projects: NOT FOUND in reviewed sources. ## 8. Three grounded conversation openers 1. Hook: building Probook’s GTM organization. “You’ve said you’re ‘building a world-class GTM organization’ and are hiring SDRs, Commercial AEs, Strategic AEs, and Solutions Consultants—what part of the system are you designing first?” Evidence: Aaron’s announcement. URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_excited-to-finally-share-what-ive-been-activity-7472702212801056768-sbVT 2. Hook: relationship-led selling. “Your SaaS-sales lesson was that prospects buy from people they ‘like, relate to, or aspire to emulate.’ How do you turn that principle into coaching behavior for your five-plus sellers?” Evidence: Aaron’s sales-leadership post and profile. URLs: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_saassales-salesleadership-relationshipbuilding-activity-7211858644965978113-UIvD and https://www.linkedin.com/in/aaronloganchurba 3. Hook: precision and objective metrics. “You’ve written that technology leaders should be ‘planning with precision,’ while Probook’s customer story references dispatching based on ‘objective metrics.’ Which metrics are most useful in proving value during an enterprise evaluation?” Evidence: Aaron’s technology-planning post and Probook case study. URLs: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aaronloganchurba_2026-it-security-budget-planning-activity-7394430474065956865-UUuf and https://www.probook.ai/case-studies/tr-miller ## Evidence limitations The strongest identity and career evidence is LinkedIn, including a structured profile extract, while the strongest current-scope evidence is Aaron’s own Probook announcement and Probook’s announcement. No public source reviewed supplied complete role-by-role responsibilities for every earlier position, named GTM tools, a formal buying methodology, direct-report names, explicit reporting lines for open roles, or a complete inventory of talks/podcasts. Those items are marked NOT FOUND rather than inferred. Third-party profile aggregation was used only as a weak corroborating index and is labelled indirectly by its nature; the me.sh result itself says it is a “LinkedIn, Twitter” profile summary and was not used to establish unique identity or sensitive facts. URL: https://me.sh/profile/aaron-churba

_request.query:
Produce an exhaustive, cited markdown profile of Aaron Churba (Director of Sales & Development at Probook):

1. IDENTITY CONFIRMATION — the primary sources that tie this exact person to Probook and this
   exact title, with dates. List the same-name people you excluded.
2. CAREER — every role with organisation, title and start/end dates, and what they were
   responsible for at each. Highlight anything to do with outbound sales, demand generation,
   account-based marketing, target-account list building, sales development or GTM tooling.
3. EDUCATION — institutions, degrees, dates, and any post-graduate or professional programmes.
4. PUBLIC WRITING, TALKS AND PODCASTS — every post, article, byline, webinar, panel or podcast
   appearance you can find, with title, venue, date and URL. Quote the most substantive one.
5. WHAT THEY OWN AT PROBOOK TODAY — scope of the role, who reports to them, which open Probook
   roles report into them, and what they have publicly said about what they are building.
6. HOW THEY THINK AND BUY — evidence about how they evaluate and purchase software: tools they
   have publicly praised or criticised, methodologies they advocate, their stated metrics, and
   their communication style (quote them).
7. NON-SENSITIVE PERSONAL HOOKS — publicly stated interests, hobbies, sports, schools, awards,
   volunteering, side projects. Nothing from the compliance exclusion list.
8. THREE GROUNDED CONVERSATION OPENERS — each must name the exact hook it uses and the URL that
   evidences it. No opener may rest on an unsourced fact.
_request.systemPrompt:
You are researching ONE named professional for a B2B buying-committee dossier.

TARGET LOCK — the ONLY subject is:
  Aaron Churba, currently Director of Sales & Development at Probook (probook.ai), the AI operating system for home-services
  businesses (plumbing / HVAC / electrical), headquartered in New York, NY.
  LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/aaronloganchurba
  Known employment history (already verified, use it to disambiguate): Probook (Director of Sales & Development, since Feb 2026), Bite (Director of Sales / Advisor), Zip Security (Director of Sales), Electric (Manager, Sales / Senior AE)

Any person with the same or a similar name who does NOT match that employment history is a
DIFFERENT PERSON. Name every same-name person you encountered and discarded, and say why.

COMPLIANCE CHARTER — hard exclusions. Do NOT collect, report, quote or allude to: health or
medical information, religion or religious activity, political opinions or affiliation, sexual
orientation, racial or ethnic origin, trade-union membership, criminal matters, family or
bereavement details, home address, personal phone number or personal email address, or anything
about their children. If a source contains such material, skip it and say you skipped it. Only
professionally-public and clearly non-sensitive personal material is in scope.

RULES: every assertion carries a verbatim quote and its URL. Write "NOT FOUND" rather than
guessing. Prefer the person's own words (their posts, talks, interviews, bylines) over third-party
profiles. Aggregator/people-directory pages are the weakest evidence and must be labelled as such.

report.description: The exhaustive cited markdown profile answering every numbered section, with a verbatim quote and URL behind every assertion and explicit NOT FOUND markers.
